Lucy Gray did not finish it. Haymitch did not finish it. Katniss did not even really finish it, not cleanly.

Lucy Gray was the first wound. She survived the Games by singing, by being clever, by refusing to become what Snow wanted. She did not bring down the Capitol. She just disappeared into the woods and left a story behind.

Haymitch carried that story. He won his Games by being clever too, but the Capitol punished him for it by killing everyone he loved. He spent 25 years drunk, broken, carrying the wound so the next generation would not have to start from zero. He was not a failure. He was the bridge.

Then Katniss comes along and she is not even trying to start a revolution. She is just trying to keep Prim alive. But because Haymitch was there to guide her, because Lucy Gray's story was still whispering underneath everything, she could do what they could not.

That is how revolutions actually work. The first generation survives something impossible and pays for it with their whole life. The second generation learns from it and survives a little longer. The third generation finally gets to finish it, but only because the first two bled for it.

Haymitch never got to be free. Lucy Gray never got to be free. Katniss barely gets to be free at the end, and even then she is still haunted.

But without them, there is no free Panem.

Carrying the wound is not failure. Carrying the wound is what makes the revolution possible.
